description:
## Goal

Give every logical source one stable typed owner and every accepted text an immutable provenance version, while making failed compiler attempts complete into the existing dependency authority. Source replacement, definition ownership, generated callable ownership and failure ownership are one atomic boundary because no partial combination can preserve accepted source, exact derived withdrawal and diagnostics.

## Public contract

- submit_source creates a new owner. A second owner for the same function, module, struct, macro or type is a conflict even when its declaration is equivalent.
- replace_source(owner, text) is the only edit operation.
- Identical text is a no-op: retain the accepted version, allocations and generations.
- A rejected replacement leaves the entire prior accepted version current.
- Once a new source version is accepted, a failing downstream derivation withdraws its stale claims, retains exactly the observations made before failure, and owns its immutable diagnostic. Unchanged failure does no work; relevant dependency movement wakes it once.
- Atomic acceptance transfers ownership and invalidates exact derived ground; it does not eagerly lower cold functions or build products.
- Old versions remain only while exact diagnostic/artifact owners retain them.

## One authority

Use existing World definition/declaration stores and scheduler publisher/read/wait frontiers. Declaration body, references, owner and provenance form one authoritative value. ModuleId, FunctionId, TypeName and generated callable identities are typed semantic identities; filenames, spans, display labels, insertion order and raw IDs are never ownership.

Generated callable identity is semantic code/capture identity owned by its lexical definition and separated from diagnostic span. Retained old closures continue to name their old immutable denotation. Equal current denotations may reuse code identity without conflating provenance.

A completed attempt returns one typed outcome containing its actual fact/product observations plus Complete, Blocked or Failed diagnostic state. Do not add a failed-job registry, retry queue, rollback World, source-state mirror, winner map, domain-specific owner registry or global scan.

## Absorbed correctness contracts

- fz-kdt.24: late duplicate global functions cannot evade ownership after the first source scoped.
- fz-kdt.30: a second module owner cannot overwrite the first or shadow a lazy reserved runtime module.
- fz-kdt.32: requester-owned struct expectations withdraw exactly when explicit replacement removes them.
- fz-tfn.53: type declaration body and references publish atomically under one source owner.
- fz-tfn.45: generated callable identity remains coherent across location edits, sibling insertion/reorder, body change and retained old closures.
- fz-tfn.46: failed attempts retain actual reads, withdraw stale claims, preserve diagnostics and reawaken exactly on relevant movement.

## Required deletion

Delete implicit fresh-submit replacement; demand-time whole-code duplicate discovery; module/type overwrite paths; append-only historical requester obligations; separate type-reference mirrors; span/display-based callable identity; fatal exits that discard reads; invented producers; provisional refresh adapters; rollback/reconciliation stores; compatibility APIs and stale tests/docs.

## TDD and acceptance

At the public API prove distinct-owner conflicts, same-owner identical and changed replacement, functions/modules/types/structs/macros, lazy runtime reservation, macro-generated declarations, generated lambdas, retained old diagnostics/artifacts, Blocked then Failed, prior success then failure, shared publishers, successful recomputation after a relevant correction, unchanged/unrelated zero requested-root work, and current provenance. Full relevant deterministic, semantic, product and three-door gates pass.

## Atomic supported-publication boundary

Source acceptance, attempt completion, typed contribution publication, and recursive support are one step. Splitting them would leave a period in which stale aggregate content can reproduce from a cycle and become indistinguishable from independently grounded content.

Observed reads are invalidation dependencies, not semantic support. For every independently justified contributed alternative, the producer must preserve its owner-qualified source justification and exact operand bindings before a join erases that distinction. Alternatives are OR; jointly required semantic evidence is AND. A source-origin label alone is insufficient because removing a forwarding/transform edge must withdraw the downstream alternative even while its origin remains.

The existing World domain store remains the one value authority. The completed typed outcome carries authoritative contribution/support changes through the existing job identity; the scheduler routes those precise edges and does not infer content support from key reachability, finality, a generic source-body read, or ProductMemo membership. Do not resurrect per-derivation publisher identity, add another flow body, copy LoweredBody meaning, or introduce a private SCC/cone/reconstruction/rollback/support-value store.

The chosen representation must be proved against real `ReturnType` and `ActivationInputs` production consumers before it is generalized. The current generic `JoinContribution` interface cannot subtract an unsupported part of an opaque joined value, so no generic support substrate may be introduced without a bounded final-consumer-owned algebra used in this commit.

Required recursive law:

```text
A = seed union B
B = A
```

Removing the last source justification retracts A and B to bottom. With independent `y`, removing `x` retains exactly `y`. The same holds when a present seed changes `{x,y}` to `{y}`, and when a forwarding edge disappears while the source alternative remains.

Additional TDD requirements:

- one publisher contributes independently grounded `x` and cyclic-only `y`: retain `x`, retract `y`;
- removing one of two equal grounded publishers preserves the value allocation/revision; removing the second retracts it;
- accepted replacement followed by Blocked cannot reuse the prior version's claims as support;
- success followed by Failed retains actual attempted reads and immutable diagnostics while withdrawing stale claims; unchanged/unrelated input performs no retry;
- retract then reappear leaves no stale `ActivationInputs` row or `ReturnType`, and revision zero is minted only from actual bottom;
- an edit that reproduces identically supported content retains allocation/generation and wakes no value reader;
- FIFO, LIFO, and permuted admission produce identical answers and exact wake causes.

Delete preserved old activation frontiers, absent-Activation standing-claim replay, stale typed-slot resurrection paths, and rebase rules only where the new authority makes them unnecessary. Finality remains a separate quiescence law and is not deleted merely because content support becomes exact.

This section absorbs the valid contract of `fz-kdt.213`; that ticket's former scheduler-metadata-only plan is invalid and must not be restored.
title: Atomically own source replacement, support, and failed derivations
